about: Claims of the Thinking length investigation, generated from the results by tools/build_findings.py. Each evidence entry names a repository file and an RFC 6901 JSON pointer; 'value' is what the pointer resolved to at build time. tools/verify.py re-resolves every pointer and recomputes entries that carry 'recompute' from the per-reply tables.

status_vocabulary.measurement: frozen rule: protocol and decision rule frozen (hashes in the run's protocol/FROZEN.json) before the first request
status_vocabulary.measurement: post hoc: computed from frozen-run data after the run; not part of any decision rule
status_vocabulary.measurement: descriptive: counted from frozen-run data; not part of any decision rule
status_vocabulary.exploratory: run kind exploratory: useful evidence, not a frozen comparison
status_vocabulary.source reading: read in source code and logs, no measurement

conventions.interval: 95% bootstrap over the unit in ci_over (percentile), 4,000 draws; each run's seed is in its protocol and in recompute.bootstrap
conventions.detected: interval excludes the null (1 for ratios, 0 for differences)
conventions.pointers: RFC 6901: split on '/', then replace '~1' with '/' and '~0' with '~' (keys such as 'C-K6x/V-BF16' contain a slash)

definitions.finished: finish_reason == 'stop' and hit_cap == False (a reply that ended on its own under the 130,048-token cap)
definitions.reasoning_tokens: tokens of the reasoning text, by re-tokenizing it with the model's tokenizer
definitions.seed_paired_ratio: for each (prompt, rep) where both arms finished: log(reasoning tokens A / B); ratio = exp(mean over all such pairs); interval: bootstrap over prompts (resample prompts with replacement, pool their pairs)
definitions.bootstrap_draws: rng = random.Random(seed); each draw: rng.choice(sorted prompt list) repeated once per prompt, mean of the pooled log ratios; sort the 4,000 draw means; interval = exp of values at indices 100 and 3899
definitions.cross_engine_ratio: post hoc: for each (prompt, rep) where both finished: log(A / B); mean within each prompt; mean over prompts; exp. Each prompt weighs the same, so a same-engine contrast differs slightly from seed_paired_ratio
definitions.engine_comparison: vLLM ratio / CuteAFD ratio = exp(mean over prompts of [vLLM prompt log ratio - CuteAFD prompt log ratio])

arms.C-K6x: CuteAFD, BF16 core converted to FP8 at load (with FP8 KDA projections, head, prefill activations)
arms.V-K6: vLLM fork, 6-bit core rebuilt to BF16 at load

findings.question: On CuteAFD v4.0.0, does the native 6-bit core change how long code replies think, against the BF16 core converted to FP8 at load?
findings.answer: Yes: 1.26x [1.24, 1.29], detected, every prompt above 1. See TL-code-engines and TL-code-fp8-arm for which arm differs.

result.name: reasoning tokens, C-K6 / C-K6x, 12 new code prompts

findings.direction: ratio above 1 = the 6-bit core thought longer

evidence.what: reasoning tokens, C-K6 / C-K6x, 12 new code prompts

findings.question: Do the two engines agree on the core's effect on code thinking length?
findings.answer: No: vLLM ratio / CuteAFD ratio = 0.79 [0.75, 0.83] (exp of the vLLM log ratio minus the CuteAFD log ratio, paired by prompt). By the reading stated before the run, the CuteAFD gap goes with how CuteAFD serves the core, not with the weight values.

result.name: vLLM ratio / CuteAFD ratio, by prompt

findings.direction: below 1 = the vLLM ratio is smaller than the CuteAFD ratio

findings.question: Which of the four code configurations thinks differently?
findings.answer: CuteAFD's BF16-core configuration (core, KDA projections, vocabulary head and prefill activations in FP8): 0.82x the vLLM BF16 core on the 12 new prompts (0.78x over all 16), shorter on every prompt; the other three sit within about 4% of each other.

evidence.what: median reasoning tokens per arm, finished replies

findings.note: Not in either frozen rule. Method (definitions/cross_engine_ratio): seed-matched log ratios over finished pairs, averaged within each prompt, then over prompts. Seed matching only pairs like with like; the unit is the prompt.

findings.question: Does the length difference change the result on code?
findings.answer: No measurable change in replies passing all hidden tests on either engine.

result.name: finished replies passing all hidden tests

findings.question: What differs between CuteAFD's two core formats besides the core's weights?
findings.answer: With a BF16 core, CuteAFD v4.0.0's launcher also puts the KDA projections (including three gate projections outside the core) and the vocabulary head in FP8, and prefill runs the MLA and MLP projections with FP8 activations; with the native 6-bit core these stay on the 6-bit kernels or in BF16.

evidence.what: source and launch-log reading with file:line references

findings.question: Which part of CuteAFD's FP8 path goes with the shorter code reasoning?
findings.answer: Being measured: the BF16-core checkpoint on CuteAFD with the KDA projections, then the head, then prefill activations switched back off FP8, on the same prompts and seeds. Not published yet.
